newsitem.title: USA: Key senator deals fatal blow to budget amendment.
newsitem.headline: Key senator deals fatal blow to budget amendment.

text.p: Sen. Robert Torricelli announced Wednesday he would vote against a balanced budget amendment to the U.S. Constitution, dealing a fatal blow to its chances of passage.

The New Jersey Democrat was the sole undeclared senator and his decision left the amendment one vote shy of the 67 required for passage. Senate Republican leaders had scheduled a vote for next Tuesday. Defeat in the Senate was expected to stall the amendment in the House for at least several months.
"I have struggled with this decision more than any I have ever made in my life...I will not cast the 67th vote," Torricelli told a news conference.

"I have approached this with enormous reverence for the constitution of our country. The constitution of the United States is as close to perfection as ever achieved in the affairs of state," he said.
Torricelli said he did not find his decision inconsistent with his campaign pledge to support a balanced budget amendment or his past votes as a House member for proposed budget amendments.
He said he would continue to support Democratic alternatives, but did not believe the proposed Republican plan met the high test needed for a change to the constitution.
